title: Twenty Questions, Smaller Edition
problem: An adversary chooses an integer from 1 through 100. You may ask yes-or-no questions, with each question allowed to depend on previous answers. What is the minimum number of questions needed to guarantee identification?

hints.text: A sequence of k binary answers has at most 2^k possible patterns.
Show six questions are insufficient, then describe a seven-question binary-search strategy.

solution.setup: Use an information lower bound and a matching constructive strategy.
solution.reasoning: Six yes/no questions distinguish at most 2^6=64 possibilities, fewer than 100, so at least seven are necessary. Seven distinguish up to 128. Repeatedly ask whether the number lies in the lower half of the remaining interval; after at most seven balanced splits, one candidate remains.
solution.sanityCheck: 2^6<100≤2^7, exactly matching the lower bound and binary-search capacity.

keyInsight: Optimal binary questions create a balanced decision tree whose leaves correspond to candidates.
recognitionCues: Adaptive yes/no identification problems invite powers-of-two information bounds.
commonMistakes: Using decimal digits and asking ten or more unnecessarily narrow questions.
followUps: How does the answer change if one response may be a lie?
